Subject: Request: private offer pricing playbook + channel passback

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo — DataPulse is close to locking an internal approval to move forward with a private offer across AWS and GCP. Procurement asked for: a short playbook that explains how Redwood structures "lift" (customer-facing discount) vs "offsets" (partner/reseller passbacks), examples of SKU mapping for multi-cloud offers, and any standard evidence we can share to satisfy our reseller team's audit (proof of margin routing).

High level asks:
- One-page explanation we can attach to our purchase request explaining how the private offer discount is applied and how partner credits flow.
- SKU example for a multi-cloud bundle (GCP compute + AWS ingress example) so our billing folks can map to their internal GL.
- Any SOC2 / audit evidence pointers or a short checklist for procurement's security review.

Can you send this by EOD Thursday? We're aiming to finalize internal approvals the following week.

Appreciate it — Sam
Sam Walker
Head of Procurement, DataPulse

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: private offer pricing playbook + channel passback

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a compact playbook and SKU mapping draft for DataPulse. Quick summary below so procurement has an immediate note to attach: 

1) Lift vs Offset (one-paragraph):
- "Lift" is the end-customer discount applied to the list price in the private offer. It shows as a reduced unit price on the marketplace invoice (what the customer pays).
- "Offset" (partner passback) is a downstream accounting allocation/credit directed to the reseller/distributor. Offsets are handled post-invoice as an internal credit route and do not change the marketplace list or the customer's invoice total; instead they appear in partner settlement runs and partner-specific invoices.

2) Typical packaging approach (two options):
- Option A — Single SKU bundle (recommended for easiest mapping): create a unified private-offer SKU that represents the combined usage profile (we provide example mapping in the attached spreadsheet).
- Option B — Dual-SKU (customer sees two line items): helpful when procurement needs separate Cloud vendor invoicing, but requires reconciliation rules (we include GL tags in the sheet).

3) Evidence checklist (quick):
- SOC2 Type II summary (redacted) — link in the playbook.
- Audit log excerpt showing partner settlement run (we can provide a sanitized CSV).
- Example invoice and partner settlement stub showing the passback allocation.

Next steps: Ben will follow up with granular margin numbers and the expected timing for partner credits (they typically arrive in the partner settlement cycle, net-30 after invoice). Irene will add the SOC2 pointer and quick redaction guidance for sharing with your legal team.

Attachments: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Pricing_Playbook_v1.pdf; SKU_mapping_datapulse.xlsx

Let us know if you want a one-slide summary instead of the full playbook for procurement.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Sales Manager — Marketplaces
Redwood Inference

Evelyn — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple clarifying questions from procurement: 

1) For Option A (single SKU bundle), how will taxes and tax jurisdiction be handled when the bundle contains resources billed from two clouds? Will the customer-facing invoice be split at the tax line or will Redwood provide a single consolidated tax calculation?

2) For partner passbacks: our preferred distributor needs a clear ERP code to reconcile credits. Can you confirm whether the offset flows include a partner reference ID we can map to our GL?

3) Timeline: if we accept the playbook and move to PO next Monday, what is the earliest private-offer effective date we can get? (need to align with our quarter close)

If you can answer inline that would be great. I can escalate to our legal if anything needs a redline.

— Sam

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Walker <sam.walker@datapulse.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: private offer pricing playbook + channel passback

Hi Sam — Ben from Partner Ops here, looping in the specifics and the ERP mapping. Replying inline to your three points.

> 1) For Option A (single SKU bundle), how will taxes be handled?

Short answer: Redwood issues a single consolidated marketplace invoice for the private offer. Tax calculation is performed at invoice time using the customer billing address and consolidated usage footprint. If local tax rules require per-cloud jurisdictional tax lines, we can emit a split tax-detail appendix (this is supported but adds reconciliation overhead). For procurement: we typically recommend consolidated tax on the invoice and providing a tax appendix for accounting.

> 2) Does the offset include a partner reference ID to map to ERP?

Yes — partner passbacks always include a partner_id and a settlement reference. In the partner settlement CSV (example attached in the playbook) you will find columns: partner_id, partner_name, original_invoice_id, allocation_amount, and GL_code. We will coordinate to include your distributor's ERP code in the GL_code field — please share that code and we will ensure the settlement feed matches.

> 3) Timeline for PO effective date if we sign next Monday

We can provision the private offer and have it active within 3 business days of PO acceptance (provisioning + marketplace approval). If you need the effective date to align with quarter close, request an activation date in the PO and we will honor it; note that partner settlements are run on Redwood's monthly cycle and partner credits will appear in the partner-run after the first full invoice (so usually net-30).

Attachments referenced: sample_partner_settlement_row.csv (in the playbook ZIP).

Operational next steps for DataPulse procurement:
- Send your distributor ERP code and preferred GL mapping (we'll update SKU_mapping_datapulse.xlsx).
- Confirm whether you want a single consolidated invoice or split appendix for taxes.
- Confirm activation date request in the PO.

If it helps I'll join a 20-minute call with your billing/AP team tomorrow morning to walk the mapping.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Partner Operations — Redwood Inference
